newsitem.title: USA: TRW posts record Q2 earnings and sales.
newsitem.headline: TRW posts record Q2 earnings and sales.

text.p: TRW Inc Monday attributed its record second-quarter earnings to strong car part sales and revenues from space and defense contract awards.

The company posted net income of $134.4 million or $1.05 a share on a fully-diluted basis, on $2.85 billion in revenues in the second quarter. The year before, it earned $130.5 million of net income or $0.98 a share on revenues of $2.57 billion the year before.
A First Call consensus estimate of 11 brokers had put TRW's earnings at $1.02 a share for the quarter.

TRW said automotive sales rose to $1.88 billion in the second quarter, up 10 percent over the same period in 1996. It ascribed the increase to revenues from acquisitions of European air bag and steering wheel operations, and from higher volume in the air bag, seat belt, steering, and engine component businesses.

TRW said a strong U.S. dollar and lower pricing in the North American air bag business moderated the sales increase. The company said automotive operating profit for the quarter increased 7 percent to $180.9 million.

TRW said its space and defense business' sales increased to $975.8 million in the second quarter, a 12 percent increase over the same period in 1996. Operating profit in 1997 rose 29 percent to $82.2 million, TRW added.
The company attributed the improvement in sales and operating profit to converting recent contract awards into revenue growth.
"Going forward, we will continue to supplement our organic growth with strategic acquisitions, outsourcing, and expansion in the emerging markets," said chairman Joseph Gorman in a statement.
Gorman noted a number of ventures that will add to the company's future growth.
TRW opened a new plant in England to produce an environmentally-friendly air bag inflator. It also expanded its electronics engineering center in Michigan, adding seven engineering laboratories.

The company also started a joint venture with Toyoda Machine Works Ltd to manufacture and sell power steering pumps to car makers in Europe. Finally, it got a $59.2 million contract to develop and produce an engineering prototype of the digital processing system for the Department of Defense's next-generation Milsatcom satellite communications system.
TRW's stock hit a 52-week high at 61-5/16 Monday morning, up 1 from Friday's close.
